A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ConfSMoE. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite formatting changes and added material.

before.justification: v2 reports original clinical and sentiment-classification results on four datasets, together with routing, imputation and complexity analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds experiments on loss-free balancing, model scaling, contrastive learning, sparsity and calibration.

M1.justification: The supervised ConfSMoE architecture and two-stage imputation remain unchanged. Appendix G.1 adds a contrastive-learning adaptation using cross-modal positive-pair confidence, contrastive pretraining and a three-layer MLP for evaluation. The explicit Top-K and attention masks otherwise clarify existing operations.

E1.justification: Both versions cover MIMIC-III/IV clinical classification and CMU-MOSI/MOSEI sentiment analysis under the same natural, random and asymmetric missing-modality scenarios. The added studies change learning procedures and configurations on retained data and evaluation tasks.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Loss-Free Balance gating (LFB) to the router comparison on MIMIC-III and CMU-MOSI. This method was cited but not evaluated in v2. The existing comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v3 introduces contrastive pretraining followed by MLP evaluation, medium and large complexity configurations, a sparsity sweep over B=1–7, and downstream-head temperatures of 0.3, 0.6, 1, 2 and 3. Expected Calibration Error is newly evaluated. These substantially extend the experimental design; the original benchmark settings remain.

E4.justification: Appendix G.1 newly tests unsupervised applicability, sensitivity to post-imputation sparsity and dependence on confidence calibration. The complexity analysis expands to three scales, and Figure 11 adds LFB routing dynamics. The original module-removal ablation is retained as Table 14, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions state three-fold cross-validation with different seeds, list seeds 2023, 2024 and 2025, and report results using the same plus/minus convention. No new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures are disclosed.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark and module-ablation values are unchanged, but v3 adds substantial scaling, LFB, unsupervised, sparsity and calibration results. For example, Table 15 reports unsupervised F1 scores of 51.70±0.63 on MIMIC-III and 40.78±0.39 on CMU-MOSI. These are new training-condition results, not improvements over v2. Table 15 also swaps the MIMIC-III TF/mmFormer values relative to retained Table 6.

T1.justification: v3 adds reasoning about differentiability conditional on a fixed Top-K mask and corrects the blanket convexity assertion by distinguishing convex loss components from non-convex network optimization. Appendix E.6 adds a derivation of mean expert importance and a claimed connection to inverse-entropy balancing. The original Jacobian derivations remain.

C1.justification: The two central contributions and missing-modality robustness claims are retained. The Introduction replaces v2's framing of missing modalities as an orthogonal challenge with an explicit hypothesis that cross-modal imputation can bias routing and worsen collapse. The abstract also explicitly qualifies agreement with Gaussian and Laplacian gating as empirical.

C2.justification: The Introduction and Appendix G.2 add explanations of imputation-induced routing bias and how low confidence reduces unreliable contributions. New analyses discuss calibration dependence and the effect of proxy-task quality on unsupervised performance. The sparse-versus-differentiable MoE limitation largely restates the earlier limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix E substantially expands implementation documentation with gating formulas, LFB update rules and implementation provenance, and the experimental load-balancing loss. Appendix G.1 specifies contrastive positive/negative construction and MLP evaluation. Original hardware, hyperparameters and access links remain. Some details conflict: Appendix E.5 uses Euclidean distance for Laplacian gating while Section 3.1 still states L1 distance.

R1.justification: v3 adds references on differentiable MoE, Gaussian gating and classical load balancing, including Puigcerver et al., ReMoE, Xu et al. and Shazeer et al., plus application citations. The original multimodal research positioning remains largely intact; the previously cited loss-free method now receives experimental comparison.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites parts of the Introduction, expands routing and imputation explanations, refines terminology and notation, and changes the author/affiliation block. New appendix subsections organize the additions, while the main six-section sequence and much of the existing prose remain.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from one-column to two-column conference formatting, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. The complexity table expands to three scales, the module ablation moves to the appendix, three new analysis tables and an LFB heatmap appear, and the notation table expands. All earlier figure images are retained; some captions are corrected.

improvement.justification: The added LFB comparison, targeted sensitivity studies and explicit implementation details improve validation and reproducibility. Section 3.1 also corrects v2's blanket convexity claim. These gains are tempered by Table 15's TF/mmFormer inconsistency and Appendix E.6's unsupported equivalence between aggregate expert-load uniformity and token-level entropy. The revision provides a limited net improvement while retaining the original benchmark evidence.
